assays.assay_description: Magnetometer-based automated head-twitch detection in mice. Dose-escalation design (VEH first week, ascending doses 1 wk apart, 5-MeO-DMT 10 mg/kg challenge at end) for LSD and 9 ergologs; additional antagonism experiments in which UCD0179 (10 mg/kg) or UCD0076 (0.6, 6, 31 mg/kg) was given prior to 5-MeO-DMT (10 mg/kg). HTR time-course also analysed (SI Fig. S14C).

application_type.evidence: "pharmacokinetic studies at 2, 5, 15, and 30 min following IP administration of UCD0179 (10 mg/kg) or UCD0120 (10 mg/kg)"; "solutions of the compounds in 0.9% saline were prepared fresh"

setup_restrain.evidence: "a magnetometer-based assay capable of automatically detecting head-twitches in an unbiased manner" — no restraint described; animals move freely in the magnetometer coil.

food_restriction.evidence: Standard short HTR test chamber; no food described in the apparatus.

water_restriction.evidence: Standard short HTR test chamber; no water described in the apparatus.

time_to_assay.evidence: "the majority of UCD0120-induced head-twitches occurred within the first 15 min post administration" — recording begins immediately after injection.

sample_size.evidence: "N = 3 to 4 female mice per group. LSD: N = 4 mice per dose; ... UCD0121: N = 4 mice for VEH and 0.1 mg/kg dose, N = 3 for 1 mg/kg dose, 10 mg/kg dose, and 5-MeO"; antagonism: "VEH/5-MeO: N = 3 mice (2 male, 1 female)"

outcomes.summary: In the magnetometer-based HTR assay, only LSD and the bicyclic ergolog UCD0120 produced significant head-twitch responses; the other ergologs (UCD0094, UCD0179, UCD0121, UCD0068, UCD0076, UCD0830, UCD0829, UCD0162) did not. UCD0179 (10 mg/kg) pretreatment failed to block 5-MeO-DMT-induced HTR, whereas UCD0076 suppressed 5-MeO-DMT-induced HTR only at the highest dose tested (31 mg/kg).
outcomes.statistics: One-way ANOVA with Dunnett's post hoc test; *P < 0.05, **P < 0.01, ***P < 0.001, ****P < 0.0001 vs. VEH (Fig. 7B); **P < 0.01 compared to VEH + 5-MeO (Fig. 8B).
outcomes.evidence: "Dose-response studies indicate that only LSD and UCD0120 induce a HTR."; "we found that UCD0076 suppressed psychedelic-induced HTR at the highest dose tested."; "We did not observe a reduction in the 5-MeO-induced HTR"

B1_num_measures.evidence: Only head-twitch counts were reported as the behavioural measure.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: "we first analyzed the HTR time course for UCD0120 and UCD0179 and found that the majority of UCD0120-induced head-twitches occurred within the first 15 min post administration (SI Appendix, Fig. S14C)."

B4_ethological.evidence: Head-twitch response is explicitly listed in the rubric as non-ethological.

B5_social.evidence: HTR is tested individually with no social construct.

B6_cognitive.evidence: HTR is a drug-induced reflexive behaviour requiring no learning or memory.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: "a magnetometer-based assay capable of automatically detecting head-twitches" — a magnetometer sensor system, not pose estimation or supervised video ML; scored 0 per rubric.

assays.assay_description: Mice freely explored an open field arena; locomotion was quantified at baseline (before drug), after UCD0076 administration (0.6, 6, 31 mg/kg), and after S-amphetamine (3 mg/kg) challenge, within a single test session (Fig. 8 C–E).

outcomes.summary: UCD0076 dose-dependently decreased locomotion in the open field and attenuated amphetamine (3 mg/kg)-induced hyperlocomotion in a dose-dependent manner. Even the lowest dose (0.6 mg/kg) attenuated amphetamine-induced hyperlocomotion despite negligible effects on baseline locomotion.
outcomes.statistics: *P < 0.05, ****P < 0.0001 compared to VEH + AMPH, one-way ANOVA with Dunnett's post hoc test.

judge_notes: All three candidates agreed on the two behavioural assays: the magnetometer-based HTR assay and the open-field/amphetamine-induced hyperlocomotion assay. No additional assays were created.

Merged all HTR variants (dose-escalation for LSD + 9 ergologs, UCD0179 pretreatment of 5-MeO-DMT HTR, UCD0076 blockade of 5-MeO-DMT HTR) into a single HTR assay per the rubric's 'same paradigm under different pharmacological manipulations = 1 assay' rule.

Excluded all in vitro/ex vivo work (radioligand binding, BRET Gq assays, β-arrestin recruitment, psychLight2 biosensor, docking) and the pharmacokinetic brain-concentration studies — none are behavioural assays.
B1 for HTR scored 0 (one measure = head-twitch count); gemma4 incorrectly assigned 1 point to the '1' category. Same correction applied to open-field B1 (locomotion = 1 measure → 0 points).
B7 for HTR scored 0: a magnetometer-based detection system is a sensor/threshold detector, not pose estimation or supervised video ML; gemma4's score of 1 was overridden.
B2 for HTR scored 1 based on the explicit within-session HTR time course (SI Fig. S14C), overriding gemma4's 'No'.
B2 for open field scored 1: Fig. 8D plots locomotion across the session (pre-drug, post-UCD0076, post-AMPH) within a single continuous session, i.e. within-session temporal dynamics.
D1 for HTR scored 1 (Multiple discrete sessions): weekly dose sessions spaced 1 wk apart with data reported for each; qwen's 'Single session' was overridden.
D1 for open field scored 0 (Single session): the three phases occur within one continuous test session on one day; deepseek4's 'Multiple discrete sessions' was overridden.
D3 for HTR scored 1 (2-7 days): VEH week + ~3 ascending dose weeks + 5-MeO challenge week ≈ 5 recording days; gemma4's '8-14' was overridden.
D2 scored 0 with low confidence for both assays: no explicit session duration is stated anywhere in the main text.
D4 for HTR scored 1: the VEH session is a recorded, reported pre-drug baseline within the same assay (Fig. 7A/B).
